---
title: "Why nonparametric Bayes?"
subtitle: "Catalog P-00 · rung 0 · after Broderick (MLSS 2016, part I)"
description: "A finite mixture must fix its number of cells before seeing data; a Dirichlet process keeps room for cells nobody has used yet."
toc: false
---

The units in a multisite study, the respondents of a test, the studies of a meta-analysis:
we usually treat them as exchangeable, so their order carries no information. De Finetti's
theorem then says the data behave as if drawn from a common distribution that is itself
unknown. A convenient way to put a prior on that unknown distribution is a *mixture*: each
unit belongs to one of several cells (clusters), and each cell has its own centre.

The question is how many cells. A finite mixture answers it before any data arrive: K = 2,
say, with weights rho_1 and rho_2 = 1 − rho_1. The widget draws such a mixture in two
dimensions: the weights from a Dirichlet distribution, the cell centres around the origin,
the points around their centres.

## What to try

- **K = 2, then K = 5.** Move N from 10 to 500. The points spread over the fixed cells and
  the bottom bar approaches the weights on top, but no point can ever start a sixth cell.
- **K = ∞.** Now the weights come from breaking a stick (the Dirichlet process with
  alpha = 1). The dashed piece is the part of the stick not yet broken. A point that lands
  there opens a new cell, so the number of occupied cells keeps growing with N, slowly.
- **Redraw** (or Enter) draws new weights, centres and points.

The rest of this ladder builds the K = ∞ case step by step: the Beta and Dirichlet
distributions for the weights, the paintbox and stick-breaking constructions, the urn and
the Chinese restaurant process for the cells, and the Dirichlet process mixture itself.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
After Broderick (MLSS 2016, part I; 2012 tutorial); the mathematics is re-implemented and
no code is copied. In the rest of the site, K_J is the number of fitted components
(occupied cells) among the J units.
:::
